summary: S. A. S. Sarma worked in Indology and held an attested post at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient in 2004 and 2024.

S. Bhaskaran Nair was an Indologist who held positions at the Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute, serving as General Editor (attested 1944, 1992) and Deputy Director (attested 1974–1977, 1986).
S. Ghosh worked in Tibetology, serving in 1982 as Librarian at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and editor for the Bulletin of Tibetology.

S. K. Ramanatha Sastri worked in Indology and philosophy, studying under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He was temporary staff at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library and served until 1938 as Junior Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras.

S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar (1871–1946) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at the University of Madras (~1895–1899), lectured at Bengaluru City University (1899–1909), and held the Chair of Indian History and Archæology at Madras (1914–1929).

S. Kuppuswami Sastri (1880–1943) studied under Brahmendra Sarasvati and Nilakanta Sastri, graduating from SPG College, Thanjavur, and the University of Madras. He served at Madras Sanskrit College, Rajah's College, Presidency College, Chennai, and Annamalai University.

S. M. Natesa Sastri (1859–1906) worked in Indology and studied at Government Arts College, Kumbakonam, and the University of Madras. Between ~1883 and 1886, he served as assistant to Robert Sewell at the Archaeological Survey of India.

S. N. Balagangadhara (b. 1952) studied at National College, Bangalore, and completed a doctorate at Ghent University under Etienne Vermeersch (1977–1991). He served as Director at Ghent University (~1991–2017) and Co-Chair at the American Academy of Religion (2004–2007).
S. N. Savadi was an Indologist who held a post at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1953 and 1969.
Shrinivas Narayan Tadpatrikar was an Indologist who held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1939 and as Supervisor of Collations in 1942.

S. Rajavelu, an Indology and history/archaeology scholar, served as Assistant Superintending Epigraphist at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 2011) and Professor of Marine Archaeology at Tamil University (attested 2015).

S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri (1893–1942) worked in philosophy and Indology, holding posts at the University of Madras as Reader in Indian Philosophy (attested 1929) and Reader and Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 1942).

S. Sankaranarayanan (1926–2014) worked in Indology, philosophy, and history/archaeology. He served as Honorary Professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1986–1999) and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.
S. Sankararama Sastri was an Indologist who served as a Pandit at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library (attested 1943) and at the University of Kerala (attested 1944).

S. Srikanta Sastri (1904–1974) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, under M. H. Krishna (~1923–1926). He subsequently held a post at the University of Mysore (~1926–1966).
S. Swaminathan worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under J. Sundaram and served at the Archaeological Survey of India until 2013 as Deputy Superintending Epigraphist.

Saba Mahmood (1961–2018) studied at the University of Washington and Stanford University (PhD ~1992–1998). She held posts at the University of Chicago (~2000–2004) and as Professor of Sociocultural Anthropology at UC Berkeley (2004).

Sabine Löhr studied Indology and philosophy at the University of Freiburg and the University of Hamburg (M.A., doctoral supervisor Lambert Schmithausen). She also served as a research assistant (Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft) at the University of Hamburg.

Saburō Hasegawa (1906–1957) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1926–1929). He taught at the American Academy of Asian Studies (~1954–1957) and held a post at the California College of the Arts (~1955–1957).

Sadajiro Sugiura (1871–1947) studied at Rikkyo University, the University of Pennsylvania (PhD), and Philadelphia Divinity School. He held posts at Pennsylvania, the Army War College, and Rikkyo University, where he became an honorary professor (1931–1932).
